verification_level: FAST plus BATCH; no STOP (no UB, ABI regression, hidden obligation or unsafe-safe-Rust API); four digest-context leak repairs, one NULL-contract correction and one failure-path secret-cleanse hardening
scope: Per-file contract audit of the ML-DSA core, the ML-KEM key/encapsulation/decapsulation core and CCM. evp/method_store.rs was deferred again as the method-store registry boundary; modes/ccm.rs was substituted from the head of the stable queue. ML-DSA/ML-KEM private keys, seeds and nonces are classified as secret; no constant-time claim is made for any file from source inspection.

files_not_run.reason: Method-store registry and OSSL_METHOD_CONSTRUCT_METHOD dispatch boundary (store locking, construct/reserve/unreserve callbacks, method cache). Deferred for a dedicated boundary audit; it remains in REMAINING-AUDIT.txt at the head of the queue.

defects.class: safety contract permits a NULL pointer the body dereferences
defects.description: ossl_ml_kem_key_reset documented `key` as 'live, or NULL' and an inline comment claimed NULL returned above, but the body dereferences key unconditionally. The authority (crypto/ml_kem/ml_kem.c:1943) has no NULL test either, so the body is correct and the contract was the defect.
defects.fix: The # Safety section now requires a live, non-NULL key and states that NULL is the caller's contract violation rather than a refusal. No code or ABI change.
defects.witness: All in-tree callers (key_free, parse, genkey, provider) pass a live key.

defects.class: resource leak on an argument-refusal path
defects.description: ossl_ml_kem_parse_public_key allocated EVP_MD_CTX before checking len, so a length mismatch returned 0 with the digest context still live. The authority creates the context inside the short-circuiting `||` condition and never allocates on that arm.
defects.fix: The length is checked first; the context is allocated only on the accepting arm. Observable return value unchanged.
defects.witness: Focused ml_kem tests (8) and the full library suite pass.

defects.class: resource leak on an argument-refusal path
defects.description: ossl_ml_kem_parse_private_key had the same allocate-before-length-check leak as M59-D2.
defects.fix: Length checked before allocation, matching the authority's short-circuit order.
defects.witness: Focused ml_kem tests (8) and the full library suite pass.

defects.class: resource leak on an argument-refusal path
defects.description: ossl_ml_kem_encap_seed allocated EVP_MD_CTX before validating ctext/clen/shared_secret/slen/entropy/elen, leaking it on every rejected argument. The authority's `||` chain allocates only after all arguments pass.
defects.fix: Arguments are validated first; the context is then allocated. Observable return value unchanged.
defects.witness: Focused ml_kem tests (8) and the full library suite pass.

defects.class: resource leak on an argument-refusal path
defects.description: ossl_ml_kem_decap allocated EVP_MD_CTX before the length/ciphertext checks; an invalid argument filled the fallback random secret and returned with the context still live.
defects.fix: The context is created only on the accepting arm; the RNG fallback still runs both for a rejected argument and for an allocation failure, matching the authority's single condition.
defects.witness: Focused ml_kem tests (8) and the full library suite pass.

defects.secondary_lines: pre-fix early returns at 1141 and 1151; post-fix cleanses at 1162 and 1169
defects.class: secret-bearing stack buffer not cleansed on failure paths
defects.description: ossl_ml_kem_genkey returned on encode_seed failure, RAND_priv_bytes_ex failure and EVP_MD_CTX_new failure without cleansing the 64-byte seed. The mdctx arm leaves a fully generated private-key seed on the stack. The authority has the same residue.
defects.fix: Every early return after seed material can be present now runs OPENSSL_cleanse(seed, 64). This is a deliberate §5 failure-path cleansing divergence; it has no observable behaviour change.
defects.witness: Focused ml_kem tests (8) and the full library suite pass.

contracts_reused: Authority allocation boundaries and release arms through the CRYPTO_* seam (OwnedBuf in src/ml_dsa/sign.rs and src/ml_kem/key.rs), including CRYPTO_clear_free/CRYPTO_secure_clear_free vs CRYPTO_free
Vector/Matrix (ptr,len) member-extent model and the #[repr(C)] layout assertions in src/ml_kem/mod.rs
CCM caller-supplied block128_f/ccm128_f callback and opaque-context ownership contract
FIPS 203/204 pointer-extent, length-refusal and zero-length-digest-update contracts
Authority-defined cleanse arms for derived seeds, masking buffers and ML-KEM secure storage
residuals: src/evp/method_store.rs remains the deferred registry/dispatch boundary.
MlKemKey::rho_pkhash is not initialised by key_new; the authority also leaves it untouched after OPENSSL_malloc, and add_storage zeroes it when dup == 0, so no path reads it uninitialised.

src/ml_dsa/poly.rs Vector::as_slice/matrix_as_slice would form a slice from NULL when the count is zero; every reachable constructor uses a positive rank and poly.rs is outside this batch. Hardening candidate, no reachable path.

The ML-DSA scratch-size arithmetic in src/ml_dsa/sign.rs uses unchecked products/additions; k/l/gamma2 come from the immutable parameter table, so no overflow is reachable. Checked arithmetic is a §3 hardening candidate.
CCM does not cleanse cmac/nonce; the authority has no cleanse arm there. Classified as a keyed intermediate residue in the caller's context, not a key schedule.
No constant-time claim is made for ML-DSA, ML-KEM or CCM from source inspection; dudect/ctgrind are BOUNDARY/SEAL work.
